question: Should OpenClaw adopt these new public plugin approval capabilities as a supported long-term SDK contract, including their deprecation and ownership commitments?
rationale: The supplied context shows a new externally consumable approval API, durable state, and broad host behavior. Without the required source/history inspection, automation cannot safely settle the permanent API direction.

options.title: Sponsor the contract
options.body: Accept the external-verification API direction after a fresh compatibility and security-boundary review against current main.

options.title: Narrow the surface
options.body: Keep the host-owned approval boundary but reduce or redesign the public plugin APIs before merge.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Pause the core PR until maintainers choose an alternative plugin or ClawHub boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the contract
recommendation.body: Accept the external-verification API direction after a fresh compatibility and security-boundary review against current main.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context ties this contributor to the proposed contract and companion implementation; current-main ownership could not be traced.
